newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia posts trade deficit in October.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia posts trade deficit in October.

text.p: After two months of posting trade surpluses, Malaysia said on Tuesday it had a 773.4 million ringgit ($306.9 million) deficit in October, partly due to the purchase of two commercial aircraft.
The monthly data followed favourable trade balances of 650.7 million ringgit in September and 600.7 million in August.

For the first 10 months of the year, the Statistics Department said, Malaysia had a trade gap of 954.35 million ringgit. News of the October deficit was expected, given the government's own forecast of a 5.2 billion ringgit trade gap for all of 1996, analysts said.
The purchase of two aircraft for 663.9 million ringgit partly accounted for the monthly deficit, the department said.

Imports in October exceeded exports in total value and growth, the department said, with imports growing at 11.3 percent while exports increased by 2.2 percent. Imports totalled 17.71 billion ringgit while exports amounted to 16.94 billion ringgit in October.

Research house Independent Economic Analysis (Holdings) Pte Ltd (I.D.E.A) said in a report on Tuesday that imports of big-ticket items, or "lumpy" imports, swung the October trade balance to the negative.
"Lumpy imports which have been absent from the external balance sheet so far are beginning to surface," I.D.E.A said.
During the first 10 months, the biggest export earners remained electronics parts, which recorded an income of 29.8 billion ringgit or 18.2 percent of total export value.
Imports in the first 10 months of this year rose by 2.3 percent or 3.6 billion ringgit to 164.04 billion ringgit compared with 163.09 billion ringgit in the 1995 period.

The department said the biggest contributor to this increase was machinery and transport equipment which went up by 2.0 percent or 1.9 billion ringgit to 98.3 billion ringgit or 59.9 percent of total imports from January to October 1996.

Malaysia's top trading partners in the first 10 months of the year were Japan (62.3 billion ringgit), the United States (56.1 billion ringgit), Singapore (54.8 billion ringgit), Hong Kong (13.3 billion ringgit) and South Korea (13.2 billion ringgit), the department said.
